=== Animation for Lecture Line 2 === # Highlight lecture line 2 self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(color_line2)) # Animate point traveling half the circumference angle_tracker = ValueTracker(0) # Define the point position based on angle def get_point_on_circle(): angle = angle_tracker.get_value() return plane.n2p(np.exp(1j * angle)) dot.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(get_point_on_circle())) dot.set_color(color_line2) # Arc to trace the path arc = always_redraw(lambda: Arc( radius=plane.get_x_unit_size(), start_angle=0, angle=angle_tracker.get_value(), color=color_line2, stroke_width=4 ).move_to(plane.n2p(0))) self.add(arc) self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(PI), run_time=3, rate_func=linear) dot.clear_updaters() self.wait(1) # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 === # Highlight lecture line 3 self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(color_line3)) # Point stops at -1, equation fades in dot.set_color(color_line3) # Replacing MathTex with Text to avoid FileNotFoundError: 'latex' final_label = Text("-1", font_size=24, color=color_line3).next_to(dot, LEFT, buff=0.1) # Replacing MathTex with Text and using unicode characters to avoid FileNotFoundError: 'latex' equation = Text("e^iπ = -1", font_size=36, color=color_line3) # Position equation in the grid area, maybe above the circle self.place_at_grid(equation, "B3", scale_factor=1.2) self.play(FadeIn(final_label)) self.play(FadeIn(equation)) self.wait(2) from manim import * import numpy as np class TeachingScene(Scene): def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines): # BASE self.camera.background_color = "#000000" self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP) self.add(self.title) # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-") lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines] self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8) self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2) self.add(self.lecture) # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side) self.grid = {} rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"] # Top to bottom cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"] # Left to right for i, row in enumerate(rows): for j, col in enumerate(cols): x = 0.5 + j * 1 y = 2.2 - i * 1 self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0]) def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0): mobject.scale(scale_factor) mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos]) return mobject def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0): tl_pos = self.grid[top_left] br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right] # Calculate center of the area center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2 center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2 center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0]) mobject.scale(scale_factor) mobject.move_to(center) return mobject class Section7Scene(TeachingScene): def construct(self): # Set up the layout for the final section title_text = "Conclusion: The Beauty of Euler's Identity" lecture_lines = [ "- A bridge between constants", "- Arithmetic meets Geometry", "- The language of the universe", "- Mathematical Elegance" ] self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines) # Main visual: The Identity itself # Replaced MathTex with Text to resolve FileNotFoundError: 'latex' # MathTex requires a system LaTeX installation; Text uses system fonts/Pango. euler_identity = Text("e^iπ + 1 = 0", font_size=72) self.place_at_grid(euler_identity, "C3", scale_factor=1.5) # Animation Sequence self.play(Write(euler_identity), run_time=2) self.wait(1) # Highlight individual parts brace = Brace(euler_identity, DOWN, color=BLUE) # Manually create Text label and position it to avoid the 'latex' requirement in brace.get_text() label = Text("Euler's Identity", font_size=24).next_to(brace, DOWN) self.play( Create(brace), FadeIn(label, shift=UP) ) self.wait(2) # Final emphasis rect = SurroundingRectangle(euler_identity, color=YELLOW, buff=0.3) self.play(Create(rect)) self.play(Indicate(euler_identity, color=GOLD)) self.wait(3)

outline.topic: The Most Beautiful Equation: Unveiling Euler's Identity
outline.target_audience: Undergraduate students or advanced high school students with a basic grasp of algebra and trigonometry.

sections.title: The Grand Hook: A Meeting of Giants
sections.content: Introduce Euler's identity as the 'most beautiful' equation in mathematics. Highlight how it connects five fundamental constants: 0, 1, e, pi, and i. Explain that these five constants come from completely different branches of math, yet they meet here in perfect harmony.
sections.example: Visualize a 'cosmic meeting' where five characters—Zero (the void), One (the unit), Pi (the circle), e (growth), and i (imaginary)—shake hands to form a bridge.

sections.title: Prerequisite 1: The Secret Life of 'i'
sections.content: Re-introduce the imaginary unit 'i'. Instead of just being the square root of -1, explain its geometric function: multiplication by 'i' represents a 90-degree counter-clockwise rotation on the complex plane.
sections.example: Imagine a drone flying on a 2D map. If it faces '1' (East) and we multiply its direction by 'i', it rotates to face 'i' (North).

sections.title: Prerequisite 2: 'e' as Constant Growth
sections.content: Explain 'e' (roughly 2.718) as the base of continuous growth. Usually, e^x represents growing faster and faster in a straight line. Establish the concept of 'growth rate' being proportional to current position.
sections.example: A magic beanstalk that grows at 100% interest compounded every single nanosecond, reaching the height of 'e' after one unit of time.

sections.title: The Fusion: Imaginary Growth is Circular
sections.content: Combine 'e' and 'i'. If 'e' represents growth and 'i' represents a sideways turn, then e^{it} represents growth that is always perpendicular to the current position. This 'sideways growth' forces the point to move in a circle rather than a line.
sections.example: A steering wheel locked to the left. The engine (e) provides the power to move, but the 'i' in the exponent keeps the car turning, resulting in a perfect circular orbit around the origin.

sections.title: Defining the Formula: Euler's Path
sections.content: Present the full formula: e^{ix} = cos(x) + i sin(x). Explain that 'x' is the angle of rotation in radians. Using the unit circle, show that for any angle x, the result is a point on the circle with coordinates (cos x, sin x).
sections.example: An animated clock hand starting at 1. As the exponent 'ix' increases, the hand sweeps along the edge of a circle, tracking the height (sin) and width (cos).

sections.title: The Destination: When x = Pi
sections.content: Apply the specific case where the angle is Pi (180 degrees). Walking halfway around the unit circle starting from 1 leads directly to -1 on the real axis. Show the math: e^{pi i} = cos(pi) + i sin(pi) = -1 + 0i.
sections.example: A traveler walks exactly half a circle around a fountain. They started at the '1 meter East' mark and ended up at the '1 meter West' mark (-1).

sections.title: Conclusion: The Identity Restored
sections.content: Rearrange the formula to its most famous form: e^{pi i} + 1 = 0. Briefly summarize why this is powerful: it links rotation, growth, and the geometry of the universe in one line.
sections.example: A final visual of the equation glowing, with the 'i' rotating a line, 'pi' defining the distance, and 'e' providing the motion, all resolving to the simplicity of zero.

storyboard.title: The Grand Hook: A Meeting of Giants
lecture_lines: Euler's identity is the most beautiful equation in mathematics.
It connects five fundamental constants in one elegant line.
Zero and one represent the basics of arithmetic.
Pi and e emerge from geometry and calculus.
The imaginary unit i joins them in perfect harmony.
animations: Highlight Line 1: Display constants e, i, pi, 1, 0 floating independently in a void (White #FFFFFF).
Highlight Line 2: Move e and i together; they begin to glow softly (Yellow #FFFFE0).
Highlight Line 3: pi orbits around e^i, tracing a circular path in the center (Orange #FFA500).
Highlight Line 4: Constants 1 and 0 appear at the end of the circular path (Light Green #90EE90 and Light Blue #ADD8E6).
Highlight Line 5: All five constants snap together to form the equation e^{i*pi} + 1 = 0 (White #FFFFFF).

storyboard.title: Prerequisite 1: The Secret Life of 'i'
lecture_lines: The unit i is defined as square root of -1.
Geometrically, multiplying by i represents a 90-degree rotation.
It turns East into North on the complex plane.
animations: Highlight Line 1: Show a 2D complex plane with a vector pointing to (1, 0) on the real axis (White #FFFFFF) accompanied by a compass [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/compass.svg] to represent orientation.
Highlight Line 2: Rotate the vector 90 degrees counter-clockwise to point to (0, 1) on the imaginary axis (Yellow #FFFFE0).

Highlight Line 3: Rotate the vector another 90 degrees to point to (-1, 0) to demonstrate cumulative rotation (Light Blue #ADD8E6) with the compass [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/compass.svg] updating its heading.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite 2: 'e' as Constant Growth
lecture_lines: The constant e is the base of continuous growth.
Growth rate is always proportional to the current value.
This creates a curve expanding faster and faster.
animations: Highlight Line 1: Display the number 'e' with its decimal expansion 2.718... (White #FFFFFF).
Highlight Line 2: Animate a bar growing upwards exponentially, with its speed increasing as it gets taller (Yellow #FFFFE0).
Highlight Line 3: Flash the height and a 'growth rate' indicator to show they are always equal (Pink #FFC0CB).

storyboard.title: The Fusion: Imaginary Growth is Circular
lecture_lines: Combine continuous growth with the rotation of i.
Imaginary growth pushes sideways, perpendicular to the position.
This constant sideways turn creates a perfect circular orbit.
animations: Highlight Line 1: Show a vector [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/vector.svg] starting at (1, 0) with a velocity arrow pointing straight up (White #FFFFFF).
Highlight Line 2: As the vector [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/vector.svg] moves, the velocity arrow stays perpendicular to it, forcing a turn (Light Green #90EE90).
Highlight Line 3: Trace the tip of the vector [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/vector.svg] to reveal a perfect circle centered at the origin (Yellow #FFFFE0).

storyboard.title: Defining the Formula: Euler's Path
lecture_lines: Euler's formula describes movement around a circle.
The exponent x represents the angle in radians.
Cosine tracks the horizontal position on the circle.
Sine tracks the vertical position on the imaginary axis.
Together, they map a point on the complex plane.
animations: Highlight Line 1: Draw a unit circle on the complex plane with the label 'e^{ix}' (Gray #808080).
Highlight Line 2: Rotate a radius from (1, 0) to an arbitrary angle 'x' (Yellow #FFFFE0).
Highlight Line 3: Project a blue segment onto the x-axis and label it 'cos(x)' (Light Blue #ADD8E6).
Highlight Line 4: Project a green segment onto the y-axis and label it 'i sin(x)' (Light Green #90EE90).
Highlight Line 5: Display the equation e^{ix} = cos(x) + i sin(x) as the components meet at the circle's edge (White #FFFFFF).

storyboard.title: The Destination: When x = Pi
lecture_lines: Set the rotation angle to exactly pi radians.
This is a half-turn around the unit circle.
We land exactly at negative one on the axis.
animations: Highlight Line 1: Start with the unit circle and a point at the '1' position (White #FFFFFF).
Highlight Line 2: Animate the point traveling exactly half the circumference of the circle (Yellow #FFFFE0).
Highlight Line 3: The point stops at '-1' and the equation e^{i*pi} = -1 fades in (Light Blue #ADD8E6).

storyboard.title: Conclusion: The Identity Restored
lecture_lines: Add one to both sides to reach the final form.
This formula links the most important constants in math.
It merges geometry, algebra, and calculus into one.
A simple expression reveals the universe's deep symmetry.
It remains the crown jewel of mathematical beauty.
animations: Highlight Line 1: Display the equation e^{i*pi} = -1 centered on screen (White #FFFFFF).
Highlight Line 2: Move '-1' to the left side of the equals sign, transforming it into '+ 1 = 0' (Light Green #90EE90).
Highlight Line 3: Highlight each character (e, i, pi, 1, 0) with a unique pulse of color.
Highlight Line 4: Scale the entire identity e^{i*pi} + 1 = 0 to fill the frame (Yellow #FFFFE0).
Highlight Line 5: Apply a golden glow effect to the final equation for a dramatic conclusion (Gold #FFD700).
